mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in FEDFUNDS above 2.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.5% and remains above for two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a high-inflation shock.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in GDPC1 below its 12-month moving average for three consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls below its 12-month moving average for three consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 70% of triggered quarters, or the relationship inverts during a supply-side shock.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in UNRATE below 5% for two consecutive months signals labor market softening, which reduces consumer spending power and corporate hiring, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 5% and remains below for two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of strong productivity growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in INDPRO above its 6-month moving average for four consecutive months signals improving industrial production, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not statistically different from zero in triggered months, or the effect reverses during a simultaneous demand contraction.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in FEDFUNDS and a fall in CPIAUCSL below 2% over the same month signals a restrictive monetary policy with low inflation, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases AND CPIAUCSL < 2% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the effect disappears when CPIAUCSL spikes above 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in HOUST and RSAFS above their 3-month moving averages signals increased residential and retail demand, which boosts earnings for construction and consumer discretionary sectors and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 3-month MA AND RSAFS > 3-month MA in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly positive in triggered months, or the effect reverses during a simultaneous spike in mortgage rates.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in PAYEMS above its 12-month moving average for two consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate hiring, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS exceeds 12-month moving average for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive in triggered episodes, or the effect inverts during a wage-price spiral.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in GDPC1 combined with a simultaneous rise in CPIAUCSL above 3% for three consecutive months signals a stagflationary environment, which erodes real incomes and profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 declines AND CPIAUCSL > 3% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during a productivity boom.
